## Overview

This week, you will learn about using generative AI (genAI) tools to help you with tasks in omics data analysis, especially coding tasks.

## Learning goals

This week you will learn:

#### Lecture A: [Using generative AI when coding and beyond](./w8a_genAI.qmd)

-   Basic background of generative AI (genAI) and large language models (LLMs)
-   What GenAI applications exist in bioinformatics and omics data analysis
-   About Ohio State's genAI adoption and approved tools
-   What options you have for using genAI tools, including for coding
-   Example prompts and outputs relevant to this course
-   Tips and pitfalls when using genAI tools, especially for coding

#### Lecture B: [Coding with an AI agent in VS Code](./w8b_claude.qmd)

-   Setting up and using the Claude extension in VS Code Server at OSC
-   Using Claude to ask questions about, write, and edit code
-   Letting Claude act as an "agent" that runs commands and works across files,
    and keeping that safe with permission settings and Git
-   Giving Claude standing instructions with a `CLAUDE.md` file

## Readings

-   @lubiana2023: [Ten quick tips for harnessing the power of ChatGPT in computational biology](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011319)
-   @pearson2025: [Universities are embracing AI: will students get smarter or stop thinking?](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-03340-w)

## Exercises & assignments

-   **Exercises**: [Shell scripts with and without genAI](./w8_exercises.qmd)

    In these exercises, you'll first write a shell script to run TrimGalore
    entirely by yourself, and only then hand it to a genAI assistant to review
    and extend. You'll use this script again in next week's Graded Assignment.

## Optional self-study material

-   [VS Code tips and tricks](../bonus/vscode.qmd) --
    keyboard shortcuts, settings, and extensions to work more efficiently in VS Code,
    both at OSC and in your local installation
-   [Using a local VS Code installation at OSC](../bonus/vscode-local.qmd) --
    connect VS Code on your own computer to OSC, without an OnDemand job
-   [GitHub Copilot in a local VS Code installation](../bonus/copilot.qmd) --
    including inline "ghost text" code suggestions, which Claude doesn't offer
-   @rahman2023: [How Much Can ChatGPT Really Help Computational Biologists in Programming?](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2309.09126)
-   @helmy2025: [Ten simple rules for optimal and careful use of generative AI in science](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013588)
-   @guest2025: [Against the Uncritical Adoption of 'AI' Technologies in Academia](https://zenodo.org/records/17065099)
